correctness.rationale: With mobile angular diffusion a>0, stationary M->S rate beta>=0, S->M gamma>0, stopped angular diffusion d>0 and zero stopped torque, the first Fourier harmonic has generator [[i omega-a-beta,beta],[gamma,-gamma-d]]. The integrable autocorrelation and exact inverse give D=v²gamma/(2(beta+gamma))*z/(z²+omega²), z=a+beta*d/(gamma+d). For beta>0 the stationary mobile fraction is strictly less than d/(d+z-a), and the bound is approached with gamma->infty at fixed z>a. Differentiation of z/[(z+d-a)(z²+omega²)] gives sign g_c(z)=c(omega²-z²)-2z³. For c<=0 this is strictly negative on z>=a; for c>0 it is strictly decreasing and crosses in the interior precisely for omega²>a²(d+a)/(d-a). The same calculation with c_gamma=d*gamma/(gamma+d)-a determines each fixed-gamma optimizer. Enhanced sup never attained by finite positive beta, and z*~[(d-a)/2]^{1/3}|omega|^{2/3} establishes strong-chirality scaling. Scope excludes stopped torque and switching costs.

value.rationale: The exact two-rate threshold d>a and |omega|>a sqrt((d+a)/(d-a)) settles whether rest periods can help a chiral swimmer at all, and distinguishes best finite protocols from an unattainable fast-switching supremum. Its cubic optimum and d/a high-chirality gain provide concrete mathematically useful performance limits for a standard stop-go model.
